name: droplet_based_pcr_thermal_cycle
title: Behavioral Modeling and Performance Evaluation of Microelectrofluidics-Based PCR Systems Using SystemC
affiliation: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Duke University, Durham, NC 27708-90291 USA
journal: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
protocol_summary: A DNA sample droplet is merged with a PCR reagent droplet (primers, dNTPs, and heat-stable DNA polymerase) and cycled through the three-step PCR thermal profile: strand separation at 95C for 45s, primer hybridization at 54C for 30s, and DNA synthesis at 72C for 90s, repeated across amplification cycles. The amplified product droplet is then read out via fluorescence detection.
